17. **How cities become free.** The ways a city breaks free of its master ("How cities become free"): conquered land not yet absorbed that revolts and breaks free ("Revolt follows conditions, not dice"); a governor who turns with the levies he raised, or a commander who keeps his army, and rules a city of his own, the new Idrimi; and a revolt with no one at its head raising a ruler from its own people ("A head rises where men lack one"). Each new free city is a power with a seat of its own, by the rules of item 11+. Built after item 13, since it needs governors and commanders, and after 11b's risen heads. Split from the city-states item on 21 October 2026, when city-states as powers moved forward to item 11+; a vassal who stops paying is free in practice already there. With revolt comes the gate opened from within, when a besieged city's hunger breaks its loyalty ("How long a siege lasts"). And an army living off the land angers its people (Haakon, 29 October 2026: "An army eating from the actual citizens stores then should make them pretty unhappy?", and to the design session's takes, "Yes, to all, expertly!"): troops taking food raise unrest by how much they take, their own king's included; every province carries unrest, the homeland too, though absorbed land starts loyal and needs far more to rise; each army buys its food where it stands by leave or takes it, as its king's order says once it arrives, but by need when it has no gold to buy with, and by its commander's choice once it has one, who may keep the gold sent for food and take anyway (Haakon, 29 October 2026: "But remember, when you say a king decides how his army supplies himself. Information time travel stoll applies. He can tell them to buy, but if he hasn't sent them enough money to buy with, they will do what they must to eat. And an army with an assigned commander (a character) the commander has the final say on following orders or not. He may keep any money meant for food, and just take instead."); and a ruler whose land was taken from remembers it as a grievance ("Revolt follows conditions, not dice" under War, "Armies need food as well as pay" under Land, people and economy). The script kings weigh buying against taking, and the item's report shows how often each is chosen and how often a homeland province rose. And the age is lengthened, set now rather than in item 18 since every later measurement reads the end of the age (Haakon, 30 October 2026: "Yes to 1."): the ending's median from 44 to about 80 seasons and the cap from 80 to 100 to 140 to 160 ("Random ending" under Victory), the omens' darkest tier at season 140; the report shows game lengths and in how many ages a Great King's war was decided (a Great King's capital taken or a Great King made another's vassal), before and after, with a new save version. Then, first, **17a, the crash and an optimization round** (30 October 2026; Haakon: "I see the game crashed now while I was watching one at high speed. So maybe need a through optimization round also."; then, of what he saw: "Got a white page with an error. Was on github", so on the live site, an error that brought the whole page down rather than a slowdown): reproduce the crash by watching whole games at the top speed in the built web app, on desktop and on a throttled phone, for as long as games run (the age now lasts about 80 seasons), recording memory, frame time and the engine worker's turn time as the game goes; find and fix the cause, whatever it is (a leak that grows with the game's history, the worker falling behind, an error), with a test that guards it, the smallest that still shows it; and make sure no error can leave a white page again: an error shows a plain screen saying what went wrong, with the seed, the season and the error to copy into a report, and a way back to the game where it can carry on; and the newest version is always the one played, without asking (Haakon: "It should update when you start game. It always pops up when I havent even started a game yet. Like why would I not want the latest version?"): today the "new version is ready" note shows on the start screen, likely because a game still held from before counts as being played, though 11c+ meant the start screen to update at once; so on opening, on the start screen and when a game is started or continued, a new version takes over by itself, and during a game it takes over at the next season by itself, reloading into the same game, with a short "Updated" line after and no question; only a new version whose rules the saved game cannot carry on in waits until that game ends, and says so; then profile the whole game, engine and drawing alike, and make it faster where it is slow, with behaviour unchanged (the same seeds replay the same, the suites and benchmarks unchanged), the numbers before and after in the PR. And the root of the stutter and the crash (Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Agreed, 100% sir!"; the improvement audit found the page holding a full copy of the game for every season, about 16 MB late in a game, and Haakon sees the map stutter at normal speed): the engine sends the page what happened each season as a stream of events, not a whole new copy of the world, and the page keeps a compact history (each season's events and what each seat knew), from which any past season is rebuilt when looked back at; the same events drive item 17+++'s playback and item 19+++'s sounds. Still hicks. hope that polish pass isn't done already, because it far from sufficed.", then "Agreed to all, expertly!"): frame times are recorded while seasons play, at normal speed and at the top speed, in the built web app on desktop and on a throttled phone, through a whole game; no frame takes longer than about 50 ms, about where a hitch becomes visible; the PR shows the longest frames and the count over 50 ms, before and after, with a short screen recording Haakon can watch. Then **17+, the opening as it stood, and the land east of the Jordan** (30 October 2026; after item 17, before item 18, one more save version): each army and fleet starts where the sources place it in 1346 (garrisons, field forces, occupiers), and each documented debt between courts starts on record, both from the dossiers with their grades ("Starting positions come from the sources" under The world); no letters or memories are written for any court. And the lands east of the Jordan go by the best-sourced reading (Haakon: "Is this the best read we have of the historical sources? If so, then i approve!"): the Shasu hold Seir (the later Edom) and the desert west of it (the later Negev), where Egypt's lists place them \[A\]; the Bashan is Ashtaroth's hinterland and the land south of it (the later Gilead) Pella's \[B\]; the plateau east of the Salt Sea, where Moab and Ammon rose centuries later, is land outside the game labelled by description, since neither name was yet in use (Haakon, 30 October 2026: "Agreed to all, expertly!"), so the Shasu no longer border Ashtaroth, Pella or Jerusalem (item 11f+'s guess, grade G, undone), the connections following the map's neighbours as 11f+ set them. And every place takes its own name ("Places by their own names" under The world; Haakon, 30 October 2026: "Agreed to all, expertly!"): the map, the seat view, every request, report and chronicle show the name the sources of 1346 use (Dimashqa, Gubla, Pihil, Urusalim), each checked against the dossiers and graded, a place with no attested name of the period labelled by description, the modern name on a second line of the province card and in the rulebook's gazetteer; the engine's ids stay as they are; and only what stood in 1346 is drawn as standing ("Places by their own names"): Shuwardata's land centred on Gath, not Hebron, and Nesa a land with no great town; and every town's people as it stood in 1346, not at its height (Haakon: "All that was materially, we should represent as accurate as possible"): Akhetaten, still being built, at about 15,000 to 20,000, below Thebes and Memphis; Kalavasos, small and new, about 1,000; Nesa about 1,000; Gath, in Hebron's place, a town of several thousand; Tunip, its site not securely found, about 4,000 to 5,000 beside Niya and Qadesh (Haakon, 30 October 2026: "Agreed to all, expertly!", to the design session's check of all seventy towns, the rest within their dossiers' ranges); each checked against its dossier. And each king starts with a standing order to pay and feed his troops, as a starting servant's job carries his king's standing order to pay him (item 11b+), so that nothing is paid or fed without an order ("Nothing happens unless someone orders it" under Overview; Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Agree with you on 1", to the design session's reading of the README review's find that the engine paid and fed troops each season with no order): it is shown among his orders, and he may change or cancel it, paying or feeding only some units or skipping a lean season; unpaid soldiers desert and hungry ones eat what they carry and then desert, as the economy's rules already say, and the script kings learn when holding back pay is worth its price. The rulebook and the seat view say so. And everyone of 1346 who mattered but did not rule is in the game from its first season (Haakon, 31 October 2026, to the design session's list from the people dossier: "Yes, expertly for all!"; then "They should also be in the place and have what they had at that time. Represent their position as accurately as we can, not just spawn them in completely randomly. and they are all from the game start?"): the attested people the dossier marks as alive and active in 1346 who are missing from the cast become characters at their courts, among them the rival claimants (Ilirabih, Rib-Hadda's brother, at Byblos; Pu-Baʿlu and Aziru's other brothers in Amurru; Artatama II, the rival king of the Hurrians, and his son Shuttarna), the officials (Ay, Nakht, Panehesy and Huya in Egypt, the commissioners Rianap and Tahmashshi, Enlil-kidinni at Nippur, Alashiya's governor) and the men of action (Tagi, Labaya's ally; Shum-Adda and Shutatna of Akko; Abdi-Heba's scribe; Assyria's envoys kept in the sun in Egypt; the captains of the Nubian garrisons), each placed where the sources put him in 1346, holding what he held then (his post, his household and means, any men he led), never spawned at random; where the sources are silent, the most reasonable reading, graded and listed in the report. What the sources say of each is his traits, never a script. No rule is made for any of them: Ilirabih may take Byblos if Rib-Hadda fails, by the rules everyone lives by. Armed men of their own only where the sources show a person leading his own in 1346 (Haakon: "Also, some of these seems to have "bands" of their own? Should they have it at game start? And also, now that we rework province "ownership" to not be a thing, but a measure of loyalty and suppression by force, should any of these characters start with competitng loyalty to the leaders somewhere, expert?"; the design session's reading: none of these led a band then; a claimant's strength is the loyalty of people, which 17++ seeds, and the Habiru stay the bands). Queens and princes stay out as before. And the Lady of the Lions, Baʿlat-nese, who wrote to Pharaoh (EA 273-274), rules a small city-state in the Aijalon valley between Gezer and Jerusalem, near Aijalon and Zorah as her letter places her, the site marked uncertain; her being a woman plays no part in the rules. The benchmarks before and after. Then **17++, what a king can count** (30 October 2026; Haakon: "Yes to both"): the province card shows a province's town and its land apart ("about 18,000 in the town; about 650,000 on its land"), as the engine already keeps them (the town's mouths eat from its market and empty its stores in a siege; the land's people harvest, pay tax and give levies), so a capital's card no longer reads as a city of 645,350; and every count a king or a model sees is as his scribes could know it, his people as well as his last count's age allows ("Counts as the scribes knew them" under The world), the engine and god view exact; and the census ("A census" under The world; Haakon, 30 October 2026: "Agreed to all!"): scribes sent to count a province, paid and taking seasons, their count travelling home dated; counted people and measured fields are the king's answer to a province's word; counting stirs some unrest; and the king says how much he wants ("The king says how much he wants" under The world; Haakon, 30 October 2026: "Yes, please, expertly!"): grain, levy and work gangs asked either as a share, which never squeezes the province but lets it hide more the older his count and the farther it lies, or as an amount, which he gets but cannot judge, falling on the people really there (a smaller next harvest, hunger, unrest, flight) or leaving wealth in the fields; a fresh count narrows both; only a governor stands between king and province; this replaces item 10+a's tax rate; and one governor may hold several neighbouring provinces from one seat, his capital for every distance, taking only those that have become his if he turns ("Governors" under War, travel and the seas; Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Yes, then his "capital" becomes just wherever he holds seat."), the script kings weighing one trusted man over a region against several over one province each; and loyalty as one ledger ("Loyalty is a ledger" under War, travel and the seas; Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Agreed to all. Expertly."): every province's people and every army's men remember what each actor gave and took, a fair exchange neutral, credit to the hand they see, memory fading, starting low, replacing item 17's separate unrest and the slow absorption of item 5 with one rule for turning governors, commanders' armies, conquered land and revolt, the script kings and characters giving and taking by it, with use against ignore measured; the ledger never shown as numbers, a king seeing his people's standing only as clearly as what he spends on knowing allows (travellers, his governor, spies and envoys, a census); and the grant of a vassal kingship under oath to a governor or any character over the provinces he holds, as Suppiluliuma did for his sons (Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Yes, expertly!"). Whether a grant pays is the king's own sum, with no rule of its own (War, "Governors"; Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Yes, to all, expertly!"): its price, tribute and terms are whatever the two sides agree, and a script king grants only where tribute and price net him more than keeping the province would, after the frictions of distance and the risk of losing it. Scripts that grant are played against scripts that never do, on the same seeds; if granting never wins, the report says whether the scripts play it badly or the land's multiple makes land too dear to give away, a finding for item 18. The map shows it (Interface, "Who holds what, and the mood of the land"; Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Agreed with all you said!"): three steps of each power's colour for land ruled directly, governed and held by a vassal, each governor's provinces bounded by a thin inner border, and the mood of the land as a view of its own, the king's dated and possibly wrong read in four coarse steps. A handful holds nothing by itself (War, "The people defend their land"; Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Agreed to all, expertly!"): no size threshold; a move into a far weaker unit is a battle it loses by far, never a standoff; a garrison holds a town only as far as its people's ledger stands with its master; script kings fold remnants into larger armies or disband them. Whom a province obeys (War, "Whom a province obeys"; Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Yes, please, expertly!"): no province is owned by a flag; each season it obeys whoever it fears or loves most, force (troops in or near it, against its own men) plus love (the ledger), and no one if nobody's weight clears what its people accept; conquest, revolt, absorption, turning and succession are this one rule; obedience has degrees by margin; the ledger starts as 1346 stood, with its divided loyalties seeded from the sources (Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Also, some of these seems to have "bands" of their own? Should they have it at game start? And also, now that we rework province "ownership" to not be a thing, but a measure of loyalty and suppression by force, should any of these characters start with competitng loyalty to the leaders somewhere, expert?"), each graded: where the letters show a province's people leaning to someone other than its ruler (Byblos's villages gone over to the Habiru and its own men urging peace with Aziru's house; Hurrian land that followed Artatama II against Tushratta), that person starts with a share of the province's love, so a claimant's strength is real and readable from the first season; changes of hands need a clear margin and come as news with their cause; persons (kings, governors, vassals, every character) do not obey a ledger but choose by their stakes and the strategy their traits give them. Script kings use the census and judge their demands by their counts where it pays, measured against scripts that never count. **Stop for review.** Then **17+++, the season plays out** (31 October 2026; Haakon: "the player needs to feel the weight of the whole world, or it becomes meaningless to him/her.", then "Agreed, 100% sir!"): each season plays out on the map instead of jumping to the next picture. The season is the land's own state beneath the realms: snow, flood, green and drought are drawn on the ground under the realm colours, which lie over it as a light wash with clear borders so that nothing bleeds through, and the change moves (snow creeping down from the passes, the Nile rising along its banks, green spreading with the rains, the land browning from its edges); the season and drought textures are redrawn, painterly and quiet, after the period's own art, on the papyrus. Orders resolve in sequence: units travel their roads at their real pace, each drawn as what it is after the period's relics, a column as long as its men are many, dust behind marching troops, ships heeling under sail through the waves, an envoy's small caravan, and nothing teleports; battles flare as a clash with their outcome, sieges tighten, and the world acts on them visibly: storms at sea, snow in the passes, rivers in flood, an avalanche taking a column ("Winter is dangerous, never closed"). Pace by meaning, never faster than can be read: at fast speed the routine compresses while the great moments (a battle, a city falling, a disaster, an envoy's arrival) still play long enough to take in, and each season closes with a short line of what changed; top speed skips to the result only when chosen. The next season is computed while this one plays, so nobody waits and the frame never stutters. Only what the seat knows plays: a rival's army appears where it was seen, when the report arrives, and a disaster far away is news, not a scene; spectators and god view see everything move. Zoom shapes it too (Haakon: "If you are zoomed in near a unit in the waves, I want to hear it. And if I zoom in on the map, I like how Imperator makes the state color more and more transparent and you see the ground and effects under more clearly."): zoomed out, the realms' colours are full and the sound is the world's bed and the great moments' stings; zoomed in, the colours thin to a wash and then to their borders and banners, so that the ground, the season and the figures show through, and the sound comes from what is near the view (the waves around a ship, a column's march, a battle's clash), louder the nearer, with only a few sounds at once so that it stays clear and light on a phone; the map's views keep their colours at every zoom, since colour is what they show. Smooth on a phone, measured as item 19 measures it, in the busiest season, and held to 17a's bar: no frame over about 50 ms while a season plays, at every speed, on desktop and on a throttled phone, with the frame times and a short recording in the PR. Presentation only, built on 17a's stream of events; it may run beside item 18, and item 19++ then makes it beautiful. Then **17+++a, keys for everything** (Haakon, 31 October 2026: "pressing spacebar really needs to pause and unpause the game. Everything should have hotkeys for the computer quiet frankly, and Paradox hotkeys is what people are used to, so we should probably use those.", then "Agreed to all, expertly!"): on a computer every action has a key, after Paradox's own, since that is what players of the genre already know. Crusader Kings III is the base, as the closest of their games to this one, and Europa Universalis IV where it has no like, each key taken from the games' own key lists, not from memory: Space pauses and unpauses; 1 to 5 set the speed, and + and −, on the main keys and the number pad, make it faster and slower; Escape closes the window in front, and opens the menu when none is open; letters switch the map's views, as their map modes do, leaving W, A, S and D with the arrows to move the map; F-keys open the main windows (the seat, the realm, the armies, the letters, the council, the chronicle), as Crusader Kings III's F1 to F8 open its own; the wheel zooms. Each key shows in its button's tooltip, one page lists them all, each can be changed and is remembered between visits, and no key acts while a letter or a name is being typed. The phone is unchanged. Space and the speed keys come first, in the polish lane, so the live game has them at once. From then on each item that adds a window, a view or an action brings its key in the same item. Then **17++++, a small state as a seat** (31 October 2026; Haakon: "maybe there should be an option to play as one of the small states, even if that's not what represented at the front and adviced", then "Yes, expertly to all!"): any city-state's or chief's seat can be taken by a human or a model, as any Great King's can, from the same seat choice, marked as harder and not the advised start; it plays by the same rules with its own seat view, letters and council ("For every ruler played by a model or a human"), and is judged on the one scoreboard against its own start, as every power already is ("One scoreboard for every power", "Relative score"), so a Byblos that holds out and grows can win. Nothing checks which power a seat is; what the item adds is the seat choice and the seat view's fit for a small realm. Rib-Hadda of Byblos is the archive's own protagonist, begging Pharaoh for archers in letter after letter. Then **17b, every person on one scoreboard** (31 October 2026; Haakon: "What if everyone are characters, even kings... Then everyone operate by the same win condition", then "Yes, please. Experlty to all!"; before item 18, which tunes it): "One scoreboard for every person" under Victory. Kings and characters are ranked on one scoreboard by what they hold, blended half and half as a first guess with their result against par for their own start; every script and model character plays to rank as high as it can; a king dies only by a cause where he is (battle, sea, a fallen city, a knife), never by dice or age; a captured king's fate is his captor's, and he may escape by his skills; when a king dies his player is out, ranked below the living, and an heir appears only then (the sources' named heir where known, and each heir after him the next name on the record of the kings who followed, all the way down as far as the record goes, in case many generations die in one game (Haakon, 31 October 2026: "I am thinking that even the heir of heir can take the real name if it is on the record, all the way down, as far as it goes, in case many generations die during a game."); past the record, a son or brother drawn as facts, named in his region's style), scored from his accession. And a realm holds by its ledger, not its capital ("A realm holds by its ledger" under War; Haakon, 31 October 2026: "Yes, do so expertly!"): occupied provinces go to the occupier, and the rest stay while their standing leans to the heir, who inherits part of his father's standing, love and hate alike (a third as a first guess); the capital is wherever the court is, moved only as a real journey; the king commands from where he is; and the heir appears with the court or among its refugees, in a city still held or abroad as an exile with a claim. A new save version.
